disagreements.reason: The split is exhaustive, but `ATPase assay using plasma membranes from L. Lactis overexpressing human BCRP` is assigned to `human`. The raw value explicitly states an L. Lactis expression host and a human introduced transporter, so dropping the host violates the host/gene-role rule. It needs a role-qualified label retaining the literal abbreviated host (or an approved explicit taxonomic normalization), not human alone.

Both raw values explicitly state a baculovirus/insect expression system and `D. rerio Abcb4`. Renaming `zebrafish + insect` to `insect` discards the explicitly stated introduced-gene species. The supported result must retain both roles, for example `insect host; D. rerio gene` (or `insect host; zebrafish gene` only if that taxonomic normalization is explicitly approved).

The split covers all 22 values, but `X. laevis oocytes expressing human ABCG2` and `X. laevis oocytes expressing human MDR1` are assigned to `human`. Both host and introduced-gene species are explicit in those raw values; abbreviating the host does not authorize deleting it. Those records require a role-qualified label retaining X. laevis plus human gene.
